title: Supreme Court: Trump v. New York
summary: Because plaintiffs have not shown standing and because the claims presented are not ripe for adjudication, the District Court’s judgment is vacated, and the case is remanded with instructions to dismiss for lack of jurisdiction. (No. 20-366, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 592 U.S. 125).

title: Supreme Court: Shinn v. Kayer
summary: Under the deferential standard of the Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996, the Ninth Circuit exceeded its authority in rejecting the state court’s determination that Kayer failed to show prejudice in his ineffective-assistance-of-counsel claim. (No. 19-1302, opinion by the Court (per curiam); 592 U.S. 111).

title: Supreme Court: Texas v. New Mexico
summary: Texas’s motion to review the Pecos River Master’s determination—that New Mexico was entitled to a delivery credit for evaporated water stored at Texas’s request under the Pecos River Compact—is denied. (No. 65, Orig., opinion by Justice Kavanaugh; 592 U.S. 98).

title: Supreme Court: Rutledge v. Pharmaceutical Care Management Assn.
summary: Arkansas’ Act 900—which effectively requires pharmacy benefit managers to reimburse Arkansas pharmacies for the cost of drugs covered by prescription-drug plans at a price equal to or higher than the pharmacy’s wholesale cost—is not pre-empted by the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. (No. 18-540, opinion by Justice Sotomayor; 592 U.S. 80).

title: Supreme Court: United States v. Briggs
summary: Respondents’ prosecutions for military rape were timely commenced under the Uniform Code of Military Justice’s statute of limitations. (No. 19-108, opinion by Justice Alito; 592 U.S. 69).

title: Supreme Court: Carney v. Adams
summary: Because plaintiff Adams has not shown that he was “able and ready” to apply for a judicial vacancy in the imminent future, Gratz v. Bollinger, 539 U. S. 244, 262, he has failed to demonstrate Article III standing to challenge the Delaware Constitution’s political balance requirement for appointments to the State’s major courts. (No. 19-309, opinion by Justice Breyer; 592 U.S. 53).

title: Supreme Court: Tanzin v. Tanvir
summary: The Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993’s express remedies provision, see 42 U. S. C. §2000bb–1(c), permits litigants, when appropriate, to obtain money damages against federal officials in their individual capacities. (No. 19-71, opinion by Justice Thomas; 592 U.S. 43).
